title: Priority Token Buckets with Elastic Grace Windows and Deferred Degradation
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Introduce an admission controller that combines priority token buckets with elastic grace windows to improve multi-tenant fairness during regional overloads. The controller should allow short, automatic expansions of token windows (grace) for high-priority tenants, then apply deferred graceful-degradation modes (prefix trimming, partial responses, lightweight model fallbacks) when sustained overload persists. This system ties to SLOs by letting elite SLAs consume ephemeral headroom while protecting regional SLOs and providing deterministic fallback semantics for lower tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Controller enforces per-tenant priority token buckets with configurable burst and refill policies
Elastic grace window behavior documented and telemetry emitted when grace is granted (grace_granted=true, grace_duration_ms)
Degradation pipeline supports two deferred paths: (1) prefix trimming + max_tokens cap, (2) fallback to slim model variant, selectable by tenant/policy
Circuit breaker integration: region-level CB trips when regional p95 latency > threshold OR queue length > threshold and triggers degradation paths automatically
End-to-end e2e test simulating regional overload shows high-priority SLO preservation at cost of degraded lower-tier outputs
No security-sensitive configuration changes required; audit logs emitted for policy changes
proposal: Design a hybrid admission layer placed in front of the request router. Each incoming request is scored (priority, tenant_weight, estimated_token_cost, deadline). The admission layer consults a per-tenant token bucket with an observed refill rate. When tokens insufficient, check elastic grace window policy: if recent headroom usage is low and tenant is in high-priority class, grant a short grace window (ms granularity) consuming a grace counter. If grace not available, apply the configured degradation pipeline (attempt 1: trim prefix aggressively and reduce max_tokens; attempt 2: route request to slim model variant with reduced resource profile). Emit events for every decision so Console can attribute cost and quality changes to tenants and routes.
design_decisions: Use token buckets (leaky-bucket semantics) instead of pure queues to limit worst-case memory and bound admission decisions
Grace windows are time-limited and charged against a separate grace quota to prevent persistent overuse
Degradation modes are deterministic and ordered: trimming -> slim-model -> reject, to make quality predictable
Circuit breaker thresholds are region-scoped and conservative; they operate on p95 latency and queue occupancy to avoid oscillation
Telemetry: expose metrics per-priority: tokens_used, grace_used, degraded_count, cb_trip_count, avg_response_quality (synthetic evals)
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Add per-tenant token bucket storage to admission service (in-memory with RocksDB backing for recovery)
Phase 2: Implement elastic grace window allocator and grace quota bookkeeping
Phase 3: Build degradation pipeline library (prefix trimmer, token cap, model router for slim variants)
Phase 4: Wire circuit breaker to regional control plane and add triggers to admission layer
Phase 5: Add metrics, tracing, and Console surface for per-tenant impact and historical grace events
Phase 6: Run canary in one region behind traffic shaping and validate SLO preservation
testing_plan: Unit tests for token bucket correctness under concurrent refills and drains
Chaos tests: simulate sudden 5x traffic spike in single region and assert high-priority SLOs preserved while lower tiers degrade
Integration test for CB interactions: trigger p95 violation and verify degradation pipeline activates within expected latency budget
Load test: sustained overload for 30 minutes to validate grace quota exhaustion and fallback stability
Synthetic quality tests: run pre-recorded prompts through trimmed and slim-model paths and compare n-gram overlap and evaluation score thresholds
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Feature flag gated behind admission.v2 in development clusters
Stage 1: Internal canary with Redwood internal tenants and monitoring dashboards for 48h
Stage 2: Regional beta in `eu-west-1` with 5% production traffic routed through new controller
Stage 3: Incremental ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%) if metrics show stability and acceptable degradation profiles
Stage 4: Post-rollout: schedule retrospective and markrun to collect long-term telemetry for 30 days
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike prototype implemented for token buckets + grace counter; local benchmarks show <1% tail-latency overhead
2026-02-28: Design review with SRE and Runtime teams — agreed on RocksDB backing and separate grace quota per tenant
2026-03-04: First integration tests failing under high concurrency due to race in grace counter; Carlos implemented CAS-based increment to fix race
2026-03-09: CB integration prototype wired; observed stable activation on synthetic p95 violations in staging
2026-03-12: e2e canary scheduled for eu-west-1 on 2026-03-15 pending final telemetry dashboard setup
notes: Trade-offs: granting grace preserves high-priority SLOs but increases token cost; must expose cost attribution to customers to avoid surprise bills
Alternative considered: per-route leaky queues with preemption. Rejected because queues increase memory pressure and make eviction nondeterministic across pods
Open question: should grace be transferable between regions during multi-region failover? Current plan: grace is region-local to avoid cross-region blast radius
Follow-up work: integrate with Optimize to recommend per-tenant grace quotas based on historical usage patterns
